title: Why Won’t My Oven Turn On? Common Causes and Fixes

content_html:
An oven that will not turn on may have lost power, be locked by its controls, fail to detect the door correctly, or have an internal fault. The first useful distinction is whether the display has power and responds, which separates supply and control issues from heating faults without opening the appliance.

Check power and basic controls

If the display is blank, check the accessible plug or breaker and make sure there is no partial kitchen outage. If the display works, review the clock, control lock, demo mode, and scheduling features in the manual.

Reset a tripped breaker only once

If the breaker is clearly tripped and there is no heat, odor, or visible damage, move it fully off and then on once. If it trips again, leave the oven out of service and do not install a larger breaker.

Gas models need a different priority if fuel is smelled

If you smell gas, do not keep trying to ignite the oven or operate nearby switches. Ventilate or leave as appropriate and follow the gas utility or emergency procedure from a safe location.

Internal failure requires service without opening energized panels

If normal power is present but the oven still will not operate, a thermal fuse, control, sensor, igniter, or element may have failed. Do not open the cabinet to test high voltage or gas; use manufacturer diagnostics or qualified service.

faq.question: What should I check if the oven display is blank?
faq.answer: If the display is blank, check the accessible plug or breaker and make sure there is no partial kitchen outage. If the display works, review the clock, control lock, demo mode, and scheduling features in the manual.

faq.question: How many times should I reset an oven breaker?
faq.answer: If the breaker is clearly tripped and there is no heat, odor, or visible damage, move it fully off and then on once. If it trips again, leave the oven out of service and do not install a larger breaker.

faq.question: What should I do if a gas oven will not start and I smell gas?
faq.answer: If you smell gas, do not keep trying to ignite the oven or operate nearby switches. Ventilate or leave as appropriate and follow the gas utility or emergency procedure from a safe location.
